a: C is a low-level systems language foundational to operating systems and embedded software.
A pointer stores a memory address; dereference with * to access the value.
Stack holds local frames; heap is manually managed dynamic memory (malloc/free).
Undefined behavior means the language does not define the result — avoid it.
C++ extends C with classes, templates, RAII, and the STL.
RAII binds resource lifetime to object lifetime (constructors/destructors).
unique_ptr/shared_ptr manage memory automatically and safely.
The Standard Template Library provides vectors, maps, algorithms, etc.
Move semantics transfer resources instead of deep-copying (std::move).
#ifdef/#define/#endif or #pragma once prevent double inclusion of headers.
